summary: Canary rollout with pinned model causes unexpected fallback routing to quantized variant, increasing latency and token truncation
description:
Issue summary:
During a canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 for customer TradeFlow.ai, requests that should have been routed to the canary pinned variant were intermittently routed to the quantized fallback (redwood-open-7b-v2-quant). This resulted in higher end-to-end latency spikes (200-800ms additional per request) and in several cases token truncation / inconsistent streaming behavior for long prompts.

Impact:
- Affects ~12% of TradeFlow.ai traffic on dedicated pool in us-east during the canary window.
- Visible user-facing errors: incomplete responses and streaming disconnects for long requests.
- Business impact: degraded demo reliability for TradeFlow.ai (enterprise customer on dedicated).

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: df-dedicated-us-east-4
- Router version: router@2026.03.08
- Serving runtime: serving-runtime@v2.8.1
- Canary config: 5% traffic, model pinning rule active for model redwood-open-7b-v2

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Trigger a long streaming generation (~1,200 tokens) pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2 via API with canary header X-Redwood-Canary=yes
2. Observe response intermittently stalls or returns truncated content after ~512 tokens, then reconnects and resumes as a different model variant
3. Check runtime logs for serving instance selection and fallback routing decision

Observed behavior:
- Router decision logs show a mismatch: requests matching canary selector were evaluated as eligible for fallback path due to a stale capability check on node labels (capabilities: quantized=true).
- Serving instances that received traffic were running quantized variant which enforces a 512-token limit under current config, causing truncation.
- Traffic percentage to canary remains ~5% but effective canary correctness dropped to ~3% due to reroutes.

Expected behavior:
- Canary-pinned requests should always prefer the pinned variant when available; fallback to quantized variant should only occur on explicit health/capacity failure, not on label capability mismatch.

Logs / Observables (snippets):
- router decision: "request_id=af3b2e, route=canary, evaluated_labels=[quantized=true, gpu=rtx6000], chosen_node=node-17, fallback_trigger=label_mismatch"
- serving runtime: "model_loaded=redwood-open-7b-v2-quant, token_limit=512"
- console traces: spike in tail latency between 2026-03-12T13:10Z and 2026-03-12T13:50Z correlated to canary window

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support toggled canary to 2% and added a hard exclude for quantized-capable nodes in the canary routing policy for TradeFlow.ai (workaround id: wk-2026-03-12-01). This restored correct routing to pinned variant but reduced canary throughput.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Router label evaluation change (deployed 2026-03-08) introduced stricter capability checks that erroneously mark canary nodes as incompatible when quantized capability is present.
- Hypothesis 2: Model pinning precedence logic had a regression where fallback rules can override pinning during selection.
- Initial reproducer run on staging with identical router build reproduced the label_mismatch path.
- Related PRs identified that touched selection priority: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls/611

Next steps / Actions:
- (ENG) Create a minimal unit test for routing precedence and backport fix to 2026.03.08 branch. (Owner: @mchen)
- (SRE) Audit node labels in dedicated pools for stale capability flags; remove quantized=true where not applicable. (Owner: @a.park)
